details: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin convened for their first-ever trilateral talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. Discussions are expected to cover global trade, artificial intelligence, nuclear security, the Ukraine war, and the US war in Iran. This unprecedented meeting is drawing comparisons to the 1945 Yalta Conference, signaling a potential reshaping of the global order. Financial markets are closely watching for outcomes that could impact international stability and trade policies, with cryptocurrencies already showing signs of pressure due to the unfolding geopolitical developments.
title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit Amid Global Tensions

details: Gold, silver, and Bitcoin experienced sharp declines on November 18, 2026, as geopolitical tensions escalated, particularly in the Middle East. US forces reportedly conducted an airstrike on an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island, followed by Iran's alleged retaliatory strikes against US facilities in Kuwait and interceptions in Bahrain. This increasing instability, coupled with concerns over rising interest rates, has driven a broad sell-off in risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, with Bitcoin touching a three-month low at $64,500.
title: Bitcoin Plunges Amid Escalating US-Iran Tensions and Middle East Strikes

details: A US-backed Board of Peace has delivered a dire assessment to the United Nations Security Council, warning that the year-old ceasefire between Israel and Hamas in Gaza faces imminent collapse. The board cited continued fighting, delays in implementing the 2025 ceasefire deal, and Israeli restrictions on aid entry. The report emphasizes the widespread devastation and the ongoing humanitarian crisis, suggesting a potential return to full-scale hostilities.
title: Gaza Ceasefire Nears Collapse as Board of Peace Warns of Imminent Failure

details: Ukrainian forces have reportedly struck the Kerch Bridge, linking Russia to occupied Crimea, for the third time in a week, forcing a suspension of train services. This comes just hours before Russian President Vladimir Putin was scheduled to meet with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The repeated attacks on this critical infrastructure highlight the ongoing intensity of the Russia-Ukraine war and pose a significant challenge to Russia's logistics and prestige, further escalating geopolitical tensions in Europe.
title: Ukraine Strikes Crimean Bridge Again, Disrupting Russian Supply Lines

details: The US Supreme Court has rejected Custodia Bank's petition for direct access to a Federal Reserve master account. The Wyoming-based digital lender had sought to bypass intermediary banks to settle transactions and hold reserves directly with the Fed. The denial upholds a barrier for crypto-native institutions seeking deeper integration into the traditional financial system. The Fed had previously cited concerns about Custodia's reliance on volatile crypto markets and insufficient risk controls.
title: US Supreme Court Denies Custodia Bank's Bid for Federal Reserve Master Account

details: The US-led "Pax Silica" initiative in the Philippines, aimed at securing critical mineral and semiconductor supply chains for artificial intelligence, is being framed as a move to counter China's technological dominance. While promoted for economic development and job creation, critics view it as deepening US influence and potentially escalating an "AI Cold War" with China. This initiative has sparked protests in the Philippines over concerns about sovereignty, environmental impact, and indigenous land rights.
title: US "Pax Silica" Initiative in Philippines Fuels US-China AI Rivalry
